desc: Formalize the orientation feasibility criterion (Hakimi: sum d = m; for all X, sum_X d >= |E(X)|) and specialize to cycle-plus-hub, deriving arc inequalities and conditions on d_N.
Transform into counting problem over sequences with bounded cyclic partial sums (walks P and Q with window constraints).

Execute the verification script and analyze output: compare brute count vs pair count vs formula (2^N-1)*2^k for N=3..7; determine whether failures stem from (c,b)-collisions or missing sequences; tabulate corrected counts vs features of s (k, runs of 1s, gaps between 1s) to guess the true formula.

Derive the corrected counting formula/characterization (likely counting distinct (d,t) via the arc constraints with parameter t = d_N, using a cycle-lemma-style enumeration over positions of 1s) and prove it.
Implement final Python solution (target O(N) or O(N log MOD), mod 998244353) reading stdin and writing the answer.
Validate final implementation against brute force for N <= 8 over all s, and against both samples (Sample 1 -> 14, Sample 2 -> 261339902).
